objects.docstring:
@poetry/motion - poetry-motion's effects, behaviors and motion policy,
one source shipped over two channels: importmap-first (the engine pins
this tree) and this same tree as the npm package for bundler hosts.

The controllers register eagerly, as poetry-core's do: the entry imports
all of them (about 6 KB gzipped together) and registers them at once, so
a press on an effect in the first moments after paint reaches a live
controller. A lazily imported controller lost those presses: a click
that dispatched while its module was still in flight found nothing to
handle it. The animation engine and the kernels stay on demand through
loadEngine(), loadConfetti() and loadGlobe().

methods.name: registerPoetryMotionControllers
methods.docstring:
The host one-liner: installs the motion policy and registers every
effect controller on the host's Stimulus application.

return.text: settled: the controllers are registered when it returns

constants.name: CONTROLLERS
constants.docstring:
Each effect's identifier and its controller class, the map
registerPoetryMotionControllers registers.

objects.docstring:
useAnimate: one engine animation for one connect, with the motion
policy applied. The keyframes end at the element's own,
server-rendered style: an entrance animates FROM an offset TO where the
server put the element. Under reduced motion nothing animates and the
element simply keeps its style. Teardown and the Turbo cache return the
element to that style.

methods.name: transitionFor
methods.docstring:
The engine transition for poetry's options: token names for duration,
easing and spring, milliseconds for a delay.

types: { duration?: string|number, easing?: string, spring?: string, delay?: number

methods.name: useAnimate
methods.docstring:
Animates `element` through `keyframes` until it finishes or
teardown(controller). With `entrance: true` it does not play on a cache
preview or a restore visit.

params.name: keyframes
params.text: property => values, ending at the element's own style

types: { duration?: string|number, easing?: string, spring?: string, delay?: number, entrance?: boolean

objects.docstring:
useCanvas: the canvas pattern. One <canvas> sized to its box at the
device pixel ratio (core's useMeasure), a frame loop paused off screen
and in hidden tabs (useFrame), and one static frame under reduced
motion. Canvas pixels never reach a Turbo snapshot, so the cache needs
nothing; the canvas is drawn again on the next connect.

methods.name: useCanvas
methods.docstring: Drives `draw` on `canvas` until teardown(controller).

types: (context: CanvasRenderingContext2D, frame: { width: number, height: number, time: number, delta: number

objects.docstring:
useDrag: free dragging with pointer capture, an axis lock and bounds,
written to the element's translate. On release the element springs back
to its own style unless onEnd keeps it (returns true). Dragging is
direct manipulation, so it works under reduced motion; only the spring
back is skipped there.

methods.name: useDrag
methods.docstring: Makes `element` draggable until teardown(controller).

params.name: |Function,
types: { axis?: "x"|"y", bounds?: { left?: number, right?: number, top?: number, bottom?: number
params.text: onMove?: (offset: { x: number, y: number }) => void, onEnd?: (offset: { x: number, y: number }) => boolean|void, spring?: string }} [options]

return.text: stops early; teardown stops it otherwise

objects.docstring:
useFrame: a callback every animation frame, paused while the element is
off screen and while the tab is hidden. Under reduced motion the loop
never starts, and it stops if reduced motion turns on mid-run.

methods.name: useFrame
methods.docstring:
Runs `callback(timestamp, delta)` every frame while `element` is visible,
until teardown(controller).

params.name: element
params.text: the element whose visibility gates the loop

objects.docstring:
useGesture: press, hover and swipe on one element, through the engine's
press and hover (which handle keyboard presses and filter emulated
mouse events) and a swipe threshold over pointer events. Gestures are
input, not motion, so they work under reduced motion; the effect decides
what to animate.

methods.name: useGesture
methods.docstring:
Wires the handlers given until teardown(controller). onPress and
onHover may return an end handler, called on release and on leave.

types: { onPress?: Function, onHover?: Function, onSwipe?: (direction: "left"|"right"|"up"|"down") => void, threshold?: number

return.text: stops early; teardown stops it otherwise

objects.docstring:
useLayout: a DOM change animated as a layout transition through the
engine's animateView (the View Transitions API): reorder a list, add and
remove items, share an element between two places. The change always
happens; it animates only when the motion policy allows a view
transition, so never during a Turbo visit transition, under reduced
motion, or without the API. `configure` receives the transition before
it starts, to name its subjects: view.add(selector).enter(...).exit(...).

methods.name: useLayout
methods.docstring: A runner for layout changes during this connect.

objects.docstring:
usePointer: the pointer's position over an element, from -1 to 1 on
each axis with 0 at the center, for tilt, spotlight and magnetic
effects. Fine pointers only: touch and coarse pointers are ignored, and
reduced motion leaves it inert. One report per frame; onLeave fires when
the pointer leaves, so an effect can settle back to its own style.

methods.name: usePointer
methods.docstring: Reports pointer positions over `element` until teardown(controller).

return.text: stops early; teardown stops it otherwise

objects.docstring:
useScrollValue: a progress value from 0 to 1 tied to scrolling, for the
page or for an element passing through the viewport. Under reduced
motion it reports 1, the finished state, once and never follows the
scroll - right for decoration. Feedback on the user's own scrolling (a
reading-progress bar) passes follow: true and keeps following.

methods.name: useScrollValue
methods.docstring: Calls `onProgress` with the scroll progress until teardown(controller).

types: { target?: Element, container?: Element, offset?: string[], axis?: "x"|"y", follow?: boolean
params.text: [options] follow: true keeps following under reduced motion

return.text: stops early; teardown stops it otherwise

objects.docstring:
useSpring: a value that springs to each new target, interrupted and
retargeted without a jump, written to one CSS property (a custom
property or an individual transform like `scale`). Under reduced motion
set() writes the target at once. Teardown removes the property, so the
element returns to its own style.

methods.name: useSpring
methods.docstring: A spring on `property` of `element`.

params.name: element
params.text: the element whose style it writes

objects.docstring:
useStagger: one animation across a list, each element starting a step
after the last. Same contract as useAnimate: the keyframes end at each
element's own style, and reduced motion, teardown and the Turbo cache
leave every element there.

methods.name: useStagger
methods.docstring: Animates `elements` in order, `step` milliseconds apart.

params.name: keyframes
params.text: property => values, ending at each element's own style

types: { step?: number, duration?: string|number, easing?: string, spring?: string, entrance?: boolean

objects.docstring:
The one door to the vendored kernels. Each is pinned without preload and
imported nowhere statically, so a page fetches it the first time an
effect asks, and never on a page without one: the engine for the
behaviors, confetti and the globe for their own effects.

methods.name: loadEngine
methods.docstring:
The engine module, fetched once per page lifetime and configured by the
motion policy.

methods.name: loadConfetti
methods.docstring: The canvas-confetti kernel (create), fetched once.

methods.name: loadGlobe
methods.docstring: The cobe kernel (createGlobe), fetched once.

objects.docstring:
The motion policy: decided once, read by every motion behavior.

- Reduced motion: the user's prefers-reduced-motion, or data-motion on
  <html> ("reduce" forces it, "full" overrides it) for an in-app setting.
  Under reduce, behaviors jump to their end state, and the engine's own
  MotionGlobalConfig.skipAnimations is set once it loads.
- Tokens: --motion-duration-*, --motion-ease-* and --motion-spring-*
  from the theme, read at the moment of use.
- The Turbo cache: the engine writes inline styles frame by frame, so a
  snapshot taken mid-animation freezes an in-between frame, and the
  engine's complete() only lands on the next frame, after Turbo has
  cloned the page. The server renders every effect's finished state, so
  the end of every animation is the element's own style: at
  turbo:before-cache each tracked animation stops and the inline
  properties it wrote are removed, now and once more after the engine's
  next render, which would write the stopped value back.
- One view-transition slot: a document runs one view transition at a
  time, and a Turbo visit transition skips a layout animation started
  beside it. canAnimateView() is false while a visit is in flight.

The listeners are page-lifetime and installed once (installPolicy).

methods.name: prefersReducedMotion
methods.docstring: Whether motion is reduced for this page right now.

methods.name: onReducedMotionChange
methods.docstring:
Calls fn with the new reduced state whenever it changes (the media query
or the data-motion attribute). Returns the unsubscribe.

methods.name: track
methods.signature: track(animation, { element = null, properties = [], finish = null, persist = false } = {})
methods.docstring:
Keeps a running animation in the policy's care until it finishes. At
turbo:before-cache it stops, and the inline properties it writes on the
element are removed, so the snapshot shows the server-rendered finished
state. Without an element the animation completes instead (a Web
Animation, which leaves no inline style). Returns the animation.

params.name: animation
params.text: playback controls with stop(), complete() and finished

params.name: [target.properties]
params.text: the CSS properties it writes inline

params.name: [target.finish]
params.text: restores anything else it wrote (text a ticker counts), run after it stops

params.name: [target.persist]
params.text: keeps the value when the animation finishes on its own (a spring holding a lean); teardown and the cache still clear it

methods.name: flush
methods.docstring:
Ends every tracked animation at its finished state, synchronously.
Turbo calls it through turbo:before-cache, and it runs when reduced
motion turns on mid-animation.

methods.name: release
methods.docstring:
Ends one tracked animation at its finished state, synchronously, and
forgets it: an inline-animated element gets its own style back, now and
after the engine's next render; a Web Animation completes. Behaviors
release their animations at teardown.

params.text: [options] finished: it ended on its own, so only its styles go

methods.name: entranceAllowed
methods.docstring:
Whether an entrance may play now. Not on Turbo's cache preview, and not
while a back or forward visit restores a page the user already saw.

methods.name: canAnimateView
methods.docstring:
Whether a layout animation may start now: the browser has View
Transitions, motion is not reduced, and no Turbo visit holds the slot.

methods.name: visitInFlight
methods.docstring: Whether a Turbo visit is between its start and its render.

methods.name: token
methods.docstring: The raw value of a motion token, or "" when the theme does not set it.

methods.name: duration
methods.docstring:
A duration in seconds (the engine's unit) from a token name or from
milliseconds. Reduced motion is 0.

methods.name: easing
methods.docstring: An easing token as the engine's cubic-bezier array.

methods.name: spring
methods.docstring: A spring token as the engine's spring options.

types: {type: string, stiffness: number, damping: number, mass: number

methods.name: configureEngine
methods.docstring:
Hands the loaded engine to the policy: its global skip flag follows
reduced motion from now on. Returns the engine.

methods.name: installPolicy
methods.docstring:
Installs the page-lifetime listeners once: Turbo's cache and visit
events, the reduced-motion query and the data-motion attribute.

objects.docstring:
Animated list: a Turbo Stream that changes the list (append, prepend,
remove, replace, update, or a refresh that morphs it) runs as a layout
transition, so new items fade in, removed items fade out and the rest
slide to their new places. The server renders the list as it is; the
stream's own render does the change, and the transition only animates
it. Reduced motion and a running Turbo visit apply the change directly.

**Values**:
- `duration` (Number, default: 300): Milliseconds for each transition.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts wrapping the streams that touch this list.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops wrapping streams.

objects.docstring:
Confetti: a burst over the page from the server-rendered, full-viewport
canvas - on a click inside the effect (from where the click landed), or
once when it connects (trigger "load": a success message a Turbo Stream
rendered). The canvas-confetti kernel loads on the first burst. Reduced
motion, a cache preview and a restore visit burst nothing; teardown and
the Turbo cache clear the canvas.

**Targets**: `canvas`

**Values**:
- `trigger` (String, default: "click"): When it bursts: "click" or "load".
- `count` (Number, default: 120): How many pieces per burst.
- `spread` (Number, default: 70): The burst's spread, in degrees.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Arms the burst.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Disarms and clears the canvas.

objects.docstring:
Dock: the items nearest a fine pointer swell, each by how close it is,
and settle back when the pointer leaves - the magnifying launcher. Each
item springs its own --dock-scale; the motion stylesheet scales it from
the edge the dock sits on, so the layout never reflows. Touch, coarse
pointers and reduced motion leave the items still.

**Values**:
- `magnification` (Number, default: 1.5): The scale of the item right under the pointer.
- `distance` (Number, default: 120): How far, in pixels, the swell reaches from the pointer.
- `spring` (String, default: "snappy"): The spring token the items follow.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts swelling the items toward the pointer.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops swelling and settles every item.

objects.docstring:
Draggable: the content follows a drag, within its parent's box when
bounded, and springs home on release unless snap-back is off. Dragging
is direct manipulation, so it works under reduced motion; only the
spring home is skipped there. The server renders the content in place,
which is where teardown puts it back.

**Values**:
- `axis` (String): "x" or "y" locks the drag to one axis; blank drags freely.
- `bounded` (Boolean, default: false): Keeps the drag inside the parent's box.
- `snapBack` (Boolean, default: true): Springs home on release; false leaves it where it was dropped.
- `spring` (String, default: "snappy"): The spring token the return follows.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Makes the content draggable.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops dragging and puts the content back.

objects.docstring:
Globe: a dotted, turning globe with markers, drawn by the cobe kernel
(WebGL) on the server-rendered canvas. It turns through useFrame, so it
pauses off screen and in hidden tabs, and reduced motion draws it once,
still. The kernel loads when the globe connects; teardown destroys the
WebGL context. It follows the page's dark class.

**Targets**: `canvas`

**Values**:
- `markers` (Array, default: []): [[latitude, longitude], ...] for the markers.
- `speed` (Number, default: 0.3): Radians per second it turns.
- `tilt` (Number, default: 0.25): Its starting tilt toward the viewer, in radians.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Builds the globe and starts it turning.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops turning and releases the WebGL context.

objects.docstring:
Layout group: elements that share a data-layout-id are one thing in
different places, an active-tab indicator or a selected-item highlight.
When the visible one changes (a class, an attribute or a child changes
inside the group), the new one animates from where the old one was to
where it is, by translate and scale, and ends at its own style. The
group remembers each id's last box relative to itself, so scrolling
between changes does not throw the move off.

**Values**:
- `duration` (Number, default: 300): Milliseconds for each move.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Records the visible boxes and starts watching the group.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops watching and returns the moving elements to their own style.

objects.docstring:
Magnetic: the inner layer leans a few pixels toward a fine pointer over
it and springs home when the pointer leaves, through --magnet-x and
--magnet-y. The wrapped control never moves its hit area or its focus;
only the layer that draws it shifts. Touch and reduced motion leave it
still.

**Targets**: `layer`

**Values**:
- `strength` (Number, default: 8): The farthest the layer moves, in pixels.
- `spring` (String, default: "snappy"): The spring token the pull follows.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts pulling the layer toward the pointer.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops the pull and puts the layer home.

objects.docstring:
Marquee: the loop itself is CSS (the motion stylesheet), so this
controller never loads the engine. It owns the pause control: a toggle
that holds the loop still, mirrored to data-paused on the marquee and
aria-pressed on the button. Hover and focus inside pause it too, in CSS.

**Targets**: `pause`

**Values**:
- `paused` (Boolean, default: false): Whether the loop is held still by the pause control.

methods.name: toggle
methods.docstring: Pauses a running loop or resumes a paused one.

methods.name: pausedValueChanged
methods.docstring: Mirrors the paused state to the marquee and the control.

objects.docstring:
Number ticker: counts up to a number the server already rendered. The
visible digits are aria-hidden; a screen reader reads the final number
beside them. The count springs from `from` to `value`, formatted with
Intl.NumberFormat, and the server's own text comes back when it lands,
at teardown and before Turbo caches the page. Reduced motion, a cache
preview and a restore visit show the final number at once.

**Targets**: `display`

**Values**:
- `value` (Number): The final number, already rendered by the server.
- `from` (Number, default: 0): Where the count starts.
- `locale` (String): The locale for Intl.NumberFormat; the page's when blank.
- `format` (Object): Intl.NumberFormat options, as the server formatted the final number.
- `spring` (String, default: "gentle"): The spring token the count follows.
- `trigger` (String, default: "in_view"): When the count starts: "load" or "in_view".
- `delay` (Number, default: 0): Milliseconds to wait before counting.
- `animate` (Boolean, default: true): false renders the final number with no count.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts the effect for this connect.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Undoes everything this connect started, leaving the finished state.

objects.docstring:
Parallax: the content drifts at its own pace as it passes through the
viewport, by --parallax-y. It sits where the server put it when the
passage is centered, which is also where teardown, the Turbo cache and
reduced motion leave it.

**Values**:
- `distance` (Number, default: 80): Pixels of drift from entering the viewport to leaving it; negative drifts the other way.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts drifting with the scroll.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops drifting and puts the content back.

objects.docstring:
Particles: a field of slow-drifting dots on the server-rendered canvas,
optionally linked by faint lines when close - the canvas pattern
(useCanvas): sized to its box at the pixel ratio, drawn every visible
frame, paused off screen and in hidden tabs, and one still frame under
reduced motion. The dots take the canvas's text color.

**Targets**: `canvas`

**Values**:
- `count` (Number, default: 60): How many dots.
- `speed` (Number, default: 12): Drift speed, in pixels per second.
- `link` (Number, default: 0): Pixels within which two dots are linked by a line; 0 links none.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Seeds the field and starts drawing.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops drawing and clears the canvas.

objects.docstring:
Scramble: the text decodes from random glyphs into itself, left to
right, when it comes into view. The server renders the text, a screen
reader reads it once, and the aria-hidden display scrambles; the text
comes back when it lands, at teardown and before Turbo caches the page.
Spaces stay spaces, so the line keeps its shape. Reduced motion, a cache
preview and a restore visit show the text at once.

**Targets**: `display`

**Values**:
- `duration` (Number, default: 800): Milliseconds from the first scramble to the last letter landing.
- `delay` (Number, default: 0): Milliseconds before it starts.
- `trigger` (String, default: "in_view"): When it starts: "load" or "in_view".
- `animate` (Boolean, default: true): false shows the text with no scramble.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Scrambles the text when the trigger fires.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops scrambling and shows the text.

objects.docstring:
Scroll progress: a bar that fills as the reader scrolls the page, or
one element (target-id). The controller writes --scroll-progress (0 to
1); the motion stylesheet scales the bar. It is feedback on the reader's
own scrolling, so it keeps following under reduced motion. The bar is
decorative; the server renders it empty, and teardown and the Turbo
cache empty it again.

**Values**:
- `targetId` (String): The id of the element whose scroll the bar follows; the page when blank.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts following the scroll.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops following and empties the bar.

objects.docstring:
Spotlight card: a soft glow follows a fine pointer across the card. The
controller writes the pointer's position as --spotlight-x and
--spotlight-y and switches --spotlight-opacity on; the motion stylesheet
draws the glow. No engine loads. The server renders the card without a
glow, and touch, coarse pointers and reduced motion leave it that way.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts following the pointer.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops following and clears the glow.

objects.docstring:
Swipe cards: a stack whose top card drags sideways. Past the threshold
it flies off that way, is hidden, and the stack dispatches
poetry--motion--swipe-cards:swipe with { direction, card, index } so the
host can record the choice; short of it, the card springs back. The
arrow keys on the focused stack and the swipeLeft and swipeRight actions
do the same without a pointer. When the last card goes, the stack is
marked data-empty and dispatches :empty. Reduced motion still drags and
dismisses, without the flight.

**Targets**: `card`

**Values**:
- `threshold` (Number, default: 100): Pixels of drag that commit a swipe.

**Events**: `poetry--motion--swipe-cards:empty`, `poetry--motion--swipe-cards:swipe`

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Makes the top card swipeable and listens for the arrow keys.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops listening; the cards keep what was swiped.

methods.name: swipeLeft
methods.docstring: Swipes the top card to the left.

methods.name: swipeRight
methods.docstring: Swipes the top card to the right.

objects.docstring:
Text reveal: the words brighten as the text scrolls through the
viewport. The server renders every word at full strength; this
controller writes one --reveal-progress custom property, and the motion
stylesheet turns it into each word's opacity. Removing it, at teardown
and before Turbo caches the page, shows the finished text.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts the effect for this connect.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Undoes everything this connect started, leaving the finished state.

objects.docstring:
Tilt card: the inner layer leans toward a fine pointer and springs back
flat when it leaves. Two custom properties, --tilt-x and --tilt-y, carry
the angles; the motion stylesheet rotates the layer, never the outer
element. Touch, coarse pointers and reduced motion leave it flat.

**Targets**: `layer`

**Values**:
- `max` (Number, default: 8): The largest lean, in degrees.
- `spring` (String, default: "snappy"): The spring token the lean follows.
- `animate` (Boolean, default: true): false leaves the card flat.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts the effect for this connect.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Undoes everything this connect started, leaving the finished state.

objects.docstring:
Typewriter: the server renders the whole line, and a screen reader reads
it once; the aria-hidden display types it out a character at a time
when it comes into view. The full line comes back when it is done, at
teardown and before Turbo caches the page. No engine loads. Reduced
motion, a cache preview and a restore visit show the line at once.

**Targets**: `display`

**Values**:
- `speed` (Number, default: 50): Milliseconds per character.
- `delay` (Number, default: 0): Milliseconds before typing starts.
- `trigger` (String, default: "in_view"): When typing starts: "load" or "in_view".
- `animate` (Boolean, default: true): false shows the line with no typing.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Types the line when the trigger fires.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops typing and shows the whole line.

objects.docstring:
Word rotate: the words sit stacked in one cell, the first one showing,
and the controller moves data-active from word to word; the motion
stylesheet slides them. Hover and focus pause it. It stops after its
rounds, back on the first word, which is also what a screen reader
hears and what teardown, the Turbo cache and reduced motion show.

**Targets**: `word`

**Values**:
- `interval` (Number, default: 2500): Milliseconds each word shows.
- `rounds` (Number, default: 1): How many times it goes through the words; 0 keeps going.
- `animate` (Boolean, default: true): false leaves the first word showing.

methods.name: connect
methods.docstring: Starts rotating.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.docstring: Stops rotating and shows the first word.
